arxiv-2111-08723.title: Who Decides if AI is Fair? The Labels Problem in Algorithmic Auditing
arxiv-2111-08723.creator: Abhilash Mishra, Yash Gorana
arxiv-2111-08723.description: Abstract Labelled "ground truth" datasets are routinely used to evaluate and audit AI algorithms applied in high-stakes settings. However, there do not exist widely accepted benchmarks for the quality of labels in these datasets. We provide empirical evidence that quality of labels can significantly distort the results of algorithmic audits in real-world settings.

arxiv-2308-12311.title: Fast Exact NPN Classification with Influence-aided Canonical Form Thanks: 1 These authors contributed equally to this work; 🖂 {}^{\text{\Letter}} Corresponding authors.
arxiv-2308-12311.creator: Yonghe Zhang 1, 1 , Liwei Ni 2,4, 1 , Jiaxi Zhang 3 , 🖂 {}^{3,\text{\Letter}} , Guojie Luo 3 , Huawei Li 4,5 and Shenggen Zheng 2 , 🖂 {}^{2,\text{\Letter}}
arxiv-2308-12311.description: Abstract NPN classification has many applications in the synthesis and verification of digital circuits. The canonical-form-based method is the most common approach, designing a canonical form as representative for the NPN equivalence class first and then computing the transformation function according to the canonical form.

arxiv-2406-19593.title: SK-VQA: Synthetic Knowledge Generation at Scale for Training Context-Augmented Multimodal LLMs
arxiv-2406-19593.creator: Xin Su ♢ ♠ ∗, Man Luo ♢ ∗, Kris W Pan ♢, Tien Pei Chou ♢, Phillip Howard ♢, ♠ University of Arizona
arxiv-2406-19593.description: Abstract Synthetic data generation has gained significant attention recently for its utility in training large vision and language models. However, the application of synthetic data to the training of multimodal context-augmented generation systems has been relatively unexplored. This gap in existing work is important because existing vision and language models (VLMs) are not trained specifically for context-augmented generation.

arxiv-2408-16428.title: Collapsing Constructive and Intuitionistic Modal Logics
arxiv-2408-16428.creator: Leonardo Pacheco
arxiv-2408-16428.description: Abstract We prove that the constructive and intuitionistic variants of the modal logic 𝖪𝖡 \mathsf{KB} coincide. This result contrasts with a recent result by Das and Marin, who showed that the constructive and intuitionistic variants of 𝖪 \mathsf{K} do not prove the same diamond-free formulas.

arxiv-2505-22078.title: Local cubic spline interpolation for Vlasov-type equations on a multi-patch geometry.
arxiv-2505-22078.creator: Pauline Vidal, Emily Bourne, Virginie Grandgirard, Michel Mehrenberger, Eric Sonnendrücker
arxiv-2505-22078.description: Abstract We present a semi-Lagrangian method for the numerical resolution of Vlasov-type equations on multi-patch meshes. Following N. Crouseilles et al. [ A parallel Vlasov solver based on local cubic spline interpolation on patches. Journal of Computational Physics (2009)], we employ a local cubic spline interpolation with Hermite boundary conditions between the patches.

britannica-1911-hero.title: Hero (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-hero.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-hero.description: Article 'Hero' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 13), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. Ancient Greek Heroes. In ancient Greece, the heroes were the object of a special cult, and as such were intimately connected with its religious life. Various theories have been put forward as to the nature of these heroes. According to some authorities, they were idealized historical personages; according to others, symbolical representations of the forces of nature.

plos-pone-0010439.creator: H. Christina Fan, Stephen R. Quake
plos-pone-0010439.description: PLOS ONE research article. However, GC bias introduced by the sequencer placed a practical limit on the sensitivity of aneuploidy detect

pmc-10652299.title: Iron overload induces cerebral endothelial senescence in aged mice and in primary culture in a sex‐dependent manner
pmc-10652299.creator: Brian Noh, Maria Pilar Blasco‐Conesa, Syed Mushfiqur Rahman, Sheelu Monga, Rodney Ritzel, Gary Guzman, Yun‐Ju Lai, Bhanu Priya Ganesh, Akihiko Urayama, Louise D. McCullough, Jose Felix Moruno‐Manchon
pmc-10652299.description: Iron imbalance in the brain negatively affects brain function. With aging, iron levels increase in the brain and contribute to brain damage and neurological disorders. Changes in the cerebral vasculature with aging may enhance iron entry into the brain parenchyma, leading to iron overload and its deleterious consequences.

pmc-10673382.title: RF Characterization of GaAs HBT under Load Mismatch with Reverse Wave Injection Technique
pmc-10673382.creator: Yidong Xu, Yuxiu Tong, Jiangtao Su, Aiqun Liu, Isabelle Huynen
pmc-10673382.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). RF PAs need to be reliable enough to protect them from damage under load mismatch conditions. This paper investigated the characteristics of GaAs heterojunction bipolar transistors (HBTs) under load mismatch conditions using a novel reverse wave injection technique to realize large VSWR ruggedness measurement with the circle centered at 50 Ohm and optimal impedance separately to analyze the device in real applications.

pmc-10750719.title: Do Arch Supports Alter Foot Alignment in Patients with Metatarsalgia? A Weightbearing CT and x-ray Study
pmc-10750719.creator: Atta Taseh, Bedri Karaismailoglu, Samir Ghandour, Karina Mirochnik, Soheil Ashkani- Esfahani, Adam S Landsman
pmc-10750719.description: Category:Midfoot/Forefoot; Lesser ToesIntroduction/Purpose:Arch-support insoles are frequently included in the treatment plans for common foot ailments including metatarsalgia. Literature has demonstrated that insoles with metatarsal and arch support could relieve walking pain and improve patient-reported measures of function in metatarsalgia. The purpose of this study was to examine alterations in foot alignment among metatarsalgia patients who used arch support insoles.

pmc-11499068.title: A case report of cardiac rehabilitation in coronary artery aneurysm combined with acute ST segment elevation myocardial infarction
pmc-11499068.creator: Xin‐di Feng, Zi‐lin Ma, Jia‐ying Huang, Jing‐yi Tang, Yi‐hong Wei
pmc-11499068.description: Key Clinical MessageCoronary artery aneurysm (CAA), marked by diffuse or localized dilation of artery, can cause life‐threatening complications in acute coronary syndrome. This report presents a case of CAA combined with acute ST‐segment elevation myocardial infarction, successfully treated with cardiac rehabilitation exercise therapy, offering insights for clinical practice.

pmc-12625967.title: Symmetry transitions beyond the nanoscale in pressurized silica glass
pmc-12625967.creator: Zhen Zhang, Zhencheng Xie, Walter Kob
pmc-12625967.description: SignificanceMany properties of amorphous systems depend not only on the positional arrangement of the atoms in the nearest neighbor shell but also on the structure of the system on the scale of the 3 to 7 nearest neighbors, the so-called medium range order.

pmc-12681749.title: Simultaneous electroencephalography (EEG) and functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) data during an inner speech task
pmc-12681749.creator: Foteini Simistira Liwicki, Rajkumar Saini, Debashis Das Chakladar, Sumit Rakesh, Vibha Gupta, Marcus Liwicki, Johan Eriksson
pmc-12681749.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Inner speech, or covert speech, refers to the internal generation of language without overt articulation. Decoding inner speech has significant implications for brain-computer interfaces (BCIs), particularly for assistive communication in individuals with speech and motor impairments. To facilitate research in this area, we introduce a publicly available dataset comprising simultaneously recorded electroencephalography (EEG) and functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) data during inner speech production.Data were collected from three healthy, right-handed participants performing an inner speech task.

pmc-12733215.title: DNA Barcoding Protocol for Masdevallia Orchids: A Tool for CITES-Based Identification and Trade Control
pmc-12733215.creator: Małgorzata Karbarz, Eliza Lebioda, Agnieszka Leśko, Zhiqiang Wu
pmc-12733215.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background: Orchids of the Masdevallia genus are characterized by their beautiful esthetic qualities. However, they are vulnerable to habitat destruction, illegal harvesting, tourism and climate change. These extinction threats have led to the listing of all Masdevallia species in Appendix II of CITES (Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora) and their selection by the IUCN (International Union for Conservation of Nature).

pmc-13236852.title: From pilots to platforms: making digital health work for chronic disease management
pmc-13236852.creator: Do-Youn Lee, Dinesh Puri, Amit Kumar Gupta, Preeti Dnyandeo Sonje, Sorabh Lakhanpal, Sujeet Kumar Singh, Sanjay Kumar, Prashant Ramdas Kokiwar
pmc-13236852.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Digital health technologies are increasingly used in chronic disease management, yet the literature still shows a persistent gap between promising pilot projects and durable health-system value. This perspective argues that the central challenge is not a shortage of digital innovation, but inadequate care-grade integration: the extent to which digital tools are embedded within clinical workflows, workforce roles, reimbursement arrangements, interoperability, data governance, and patient support.

pmc-13250571.title: Focused ultrasound for enhancing cell-based immunotherapies in neuro-oncology
pmc-13250571.creator: Thomas Sherlock, Andrew T Thede, Natasha D Sheybani
pmc-13250571.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Cancers of the brain remain notoriously difficult to treat because of the unique and complex barriers imposed by the central nervous system and tumor microenvironment. Current therapeutic paradigms remain largely insufficient to achieve durable responses or cures. Cellular immunotherapies (CIs), including chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cells and natural killer cell therapies, represent a new class of “living drugs” that harness endogenous or adoptively transferred immune cells to target and destroy cancer.

pmc-13399052.title: Dapagliflozin does not impair microvascular hemorheology in type 2 diabetes mellitus: A multicenter randomized controlled trial (D‐PATH study)
pmc-13399052.creator: Yuki Nakatani, Nobuyuki Banba, Shoya Ono, Tomoki Turumi, Megumi Hoshiai, Takushi Sugiyama, Takashi Tomoe, Hajime Tamiya, Naoyuki Otani, Hiroyuki Sugimura, Hidekazu Ikemiyagi, Yusuke Ohya, Koji Yokokawa, Shinichiro Ueda, Yoshimasa Aso, Yasuhiro Maejima, Takanori Yasu
pmc-13399052.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). AimsSodium–glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors reduce cardiovascular and renal events beyond glucose lowering, but their hematocrit‐raising effects raise concerns about increased blood viscosity and microvascular impairment. We investigated whether dapagliflozin adversely affects microvascular hemorheology in patients with type 2 diabetes.Materials and MethodsIn this multicenter, open‐label, randomized controlled trial, 82 adults with type 2 diabetes received dapagliflozin (5 mg/day) or conventional therapy for 16 weeks.

pmc-13577270.title: Economic burden of Generalized Pustular Psoriasis in Malaysia: a multi-centre analysis of indirect costs
pmc-13577270.creator: Siew Chin Ong, Xin Qian Seah, Mustapha Mohammed, Mei Ee Tay, Latha Selvarajah, Wooi Chiang Tan, Sook Yee Michelle Voo, Yen Loo Ting, Jyh Jong Tang, Siti Nur Sharida Abd Kadir, Azura Mohd Affandi
pmc-13577270.description: BackgroundGeneralized Pustular Psoriasis (GPP) constitutes a rare yet severe variant of psoriasis, characterised by extensive pustule formation on the skin and imposes a significant economic burden. The study aimed to investigate the indirect costs associated with GPP in Malaysia, encompassing patients’ work productivity losses and out-of-pocket expenses.
